newsitem.title: UK: Soccer Investments bucks trend on AIM debut.
newsitem.headline: Soccer Investments bucks trend on AIM debut.

text.p: Shares in potential football club owner Soccer Investments Plc rose to a premium in first day dealings on Wednesday, bucking the recent downward trend in the sector, dealers said.
The shares, listed at 100p and making their debut on the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market (AIM), gained 2-1/2p to 102-1/2p by 1050 GMT.
Dealers said volume was light and likely to remain so until there was any developments on Soccer Investments' acquisition plans.
"We've got hear some news before we see any action," said one dealer.
Soccer Investments is a shell company, which has raised 10 million stg via a placing. It plans to use the proceeds to acquire a controlling stake in a British football club.

Non-executive directors on Soccers Investments' board include Sir Rodney Walker, who is chairman of the Sports Council and Brands Hatch Leisure, John Edelson, a director of Manchester United and Alan Hansen, a former Liverpool and Scotland international player.
Soccer Investments' broker, Wise Speke, said that the company will be looking at premier league and first division clubs but declined to mention any names.
"I think you could narrow it down to between six and 10 clubs from either the premier league or first division," said Neil Baldwin of Wise Speke.
The company said it has a cash back option of 96-1/2p a share should it not buy a controlling stake in a football club.
"The shares have a limited downside because if the company does not make an acquisition in the next two years, it would call an EGM and return cash to the backers," said Baldwin.
Football club shares have fallen from their highs in last two months but some analysts believe this is a healthy correction.
"Football shares are still up 19 per cent since the start of the season," said one analyst.

By far the largest club with a market capitalisation of about 420 million stg is English champions Manchester United. United's shares have slid from a year high of 737p on January 24 to 660p on Wednesday.
A victory over rivals Liverpool last Saturday, making them strong favourites to retain the prestigious premier league title, failed to boost the share price significantly.

Chelsea Village, owner of Chelsea Football Club, have seen their shares drop from a year high of 170p on February 7 to 119p in spite of reaching the F.A. Cup final, opening the door to possible European competition next season.

Newcastle United shares have more closely reflected their fortunes on the field. Newcastle's hopes of becoming Premier League champions have receded in the last month and so has its share price. The shares were 124-1/2p down from an issue price of 135p on April 2.

The possibility of relegation from the premier league still looms for Sunderland FC and the share price at 490p is only just above its year low of 480p. Some three million pounds was wiped off the value of Sunderland on Wednesday following a crucial 1-0 defeat against Southampton in a relegation battle on Tuesday night.
